:::{#exm-not-question}
#### Overlapping sets do not form a question
<!-- no-figure: the example lists two sets, with nothing to plot -->

Let $X$ be as in @exm-question.
The two [sets](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-set) $\{0, 1, \ldots, 40\}$ and $\{32, 33, \ldots, 63\}$ cover $\srcalph$,
but both hold the values $32, 33, \ldots, 40$.
They are not [disjoint](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-mutually-exclusive),
so they do not form a [question](#def-question),
and neither set is a [possible answer](#def-possible-answer).
When $X = 35$,
both sets hold the value of $X$,
so no single set is its answer.

:::
